title: Work
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Child labour is taught for protection: a child who is working too much is never shamed in class; follow the school safeguarding policy and name Childline Kenya 116.

skills.key_step: The child names the work God gave people in Genesis 1:26-28 and 2:15 (look after the garden, care for living things, be fruitful) and lists a child's roles at home, school and church.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to care for school items.
floor.question: Name one way to care for a school desk.
floor.answer: Do not write on it (keep it clean)

representations: pictures of a garden and a tree nursery
steps: Read Genesis 2:15: work it and take care of it.
List roles at home, school and church.
Pick one to do this week.

board.do: Write Genesis 2:15 and draw a garden.

board.say: Does ruling over creation mean using it up?

board.do: Wait for the child to say no, caring for it.
Fill in the home, school and church columns.

listen_for: Use them as we like, even if they are finished
misconceptions.ask: What does it mean to rule over the animals and plants in Genesis 1:26 and 2:15?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 2:15 beside it: "to work it and take care of it".

listen_for: After they did wrong, as a punishment
misconceptions.ask: When did God first give human beings work in the Bible?
misconceptions.repair: Compare Genesis 2:15 (work in the garden) with Genesis 3.

misconceptions.ask: Which one is a role a child can do at church?
misconceptions.repair: Make three lists on the board: home, school and church.

misconceptions.ask: Name one role a Grade 5 child has at home.
misconceptions.repair: Make three columns, home, school, church, and fill them only with things a ten-year-old can do.

checks.question: When did God first give people work in the Bible?
checks.answer: In the garden, before they did wrong

checks.question: Name a role a child can do at church.
checks.answer: Help keep the compound clean (sing, usher)

skills.key_step: The child tells child labour (work that harms health or keeps a child from school, such as carrying heavy loads for hours or working for pay instead of school) from age-appropriate chores, gives causes (poverty, loss of parents) and effects, and names whom to tell.

floor.prerequisite: Knows a child's roles at home.
floor.question: Name one chore a Grade 5 child can do at home.

representations: two columns: a chore that helps, work that harms
steps: Ask: is it light and safe, and does the child still go to school?
If yes, it is a chore.
If it harms or stops school, it is child labour.
Tell a trusted adult or call 116.
contexts: a child selling in the market during school hours
a child fetching water before school
a child herding all day instead of school

board.do: Draw two columns: chore and child labour.
Point at a card of a child carrying stones at a quarry.
Wait for the child to say child labour, it harms and stops school.
Write 116 and the names of trusted adults.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is child labour?
misconceptions.repair: Sort tasks by three questions: is it safe, does it suit my age, does it stop me from school or rest?

listen_for: The child learns more at school
misconceptions.ask: What is a common effect of child labour?
misconceptions.repair: Name a child who herds all day and cannot read. Ask what the child lost.

misconceptions.ask: Whom should a child tell if he is forced to work?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list of safe adults together, including the Childline Kenya line 116.

listen_for: Children who like to be lazy
misconceptions.ask: What is one cause of child labour in many places?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a family with no food might feel it must do.

checks.question: Is sweeping the room after school child labour?
Whom should a child tell if forced to work?
